baseline.answer: When `totalChars <= options.triggerChars`, masking does not run: the function returns the messages unchanged (a copy), with `maskedCount: 0`, `charsRemoved: 0`, `applied: false`, and `totalObservationChars` set to the computed total. The exact `skippedReason` value is `'below_trigger'`. Note this branch is reached only if at least one tool result exists — with zero observations the earlier check returns `'nothing_maskable'` instead.

optimized.answer: When the accumulated tool-result text length is `<= options.triggerChars`, `maskObservations` short-circuits and masks nothing: it returns a copy of the original `messages` with `maskedCount: 0`, `charsRemoved: 0`, `applied: false`, and `totalObservationChars` set to the measured `totalChars` (the spread overrides the `0` from the `unchanged` helper). The exact `skippedReason` value is `'below_trigger'`. Note this check runs only after the zero-observation case, which returns `'nothing_maskable'` instead.

baseline.answer: Non-text children such as images or binary data are never masked — they are filtered out of the collapse and preserved as-is, appended after the single text placeholder — because their size is not the problem and their loss would be silent.

optimized.answer: Non-text children are preserved as-is: the masking step filters out only the `text` children and rebuilds the tool result's content as a single placeholder text part followed by all the surviving non-text children (images, binary data, etc.) in their original order.

optimized.answer: It returns the `unchanged('failed')` result — a shallow copy of the input messages with `maskedCount: 0`, `charsRemoved: 0`, `totalObservationChars: 0`, and `applied: false`. The exact `skippedReason` value is `'failed'`.

baseline.answer: It returns a full-document fallback only when retrieval was attempted and produced no usable evidence — a `sufficiency` of `unusable` (or a `selectedCount` of 0 for callers predating that field).

optimized.answer: Only when retrieval came back `unusable` — i.e. its three-way sufficiency verdict is `'unusable'`, which the contract documents as the sole state justifying attaching a whole file. An `incomplete_declared` outcome still carries evidence and declares its own gap, so it does not earn the full-document fallback.
